name: tls-loopback
algorithm: a TLS 1.3 server and client in one process over loopback TCP, a task (goroutine) each, X25519 and TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, the server's P-256 leaf under a P-256 root checked by the client (the certificates and key are constants in each column, valid 2000 to 2200). Mode bulk: one handshake, then n MiB in 16 KiB WriteAll calls, the server reading with 16 KiB Reads and adding every byte. Mode handshake: n connections one after another, each a full handshake, one byte each way, close_notify both ways. Mode system: as handshake with the client's roots none, so each handshake is refused at the chain check (the bench root is not the system's). Prints the bytes or round trips the client counted, the server's byte sum and the failures (mk/tls-loopback.mk).

variants.name: system
notes: Item 7.13 (D-704): a handshake with roots none, the system's pool. tools/bench sets no environment per row, so the bench root cannot be the system's: each handshake is refused at the chain check and counted, on Windows by the platform's check, on Linux against the bundle the process loaded once (Mk's x509.SystemPool, Go's systemRoots). The row prices what roots none costs a handshake beside the program's own pool; its ratio is item 10's to publish. Both checksums are what one untimed run of each column printed on Windows (item 7.13's writer, 2026-11-15, `tls-loopback 3 system` and `tls-loopback 200 system`): n refused, sum 0, n failed server handshakes.

skip.c: no std TLS: C has no standard TLS library (OpenSSL, BoringSSL and mbedTLS are third-party)
skip.rust: no std TLS: Rust std has none; rustls is third-party, and no crate stands in (plan/06-m6.md 4.1)
skip.zig: no std TLS server: Zig 0.17.0's std.crypto.tls has a client only, so neither mode can run both ends in Zig

notes: Written by std-tls (status/std-tls.md). Checksums from the Go column and equal in the Mk column: bulk sums n * 133693440 (a 16 KiB piece adds 2088960, 64 pieces a MiB), handshake sums i mod 256 over i = 0..n-1.

Sockets: mode handshake opens n client and n server sockets, each left in TIME_WAIT after its close; 200 a run keeps a full tools/bench sweep (both columns, every repetition) far under the owner's cap of 10,000 sockets. Do not raise n without counting the sweep's sockets.

Go: no session tickets (std.tls builds no resumption), MinVersion TLS 1.3, CurvePreferences X25519 alone on both ends (Go 1.27's default puts the hybrid X25519MLKEM768 first, which the Mk client does not offer), and Go's suite choice, AES-128-GCM on a host with AES instructions, as the Mk client's first suite.
